latest_validation.mathematical_scope: A bounded complex unit-curve integral defines the continuous scalar-state cross-mass. The classical two-energy Lagrange identity extends by finite Fourier density to actual rough states for arbitrary complex L2 potentials. Continuous frequency dependence holds in the uniform curve norm. The punctured quadratic map limit, including frequency zero, combines with the Lagrange identity to prove the exact normalization D_prime(energy)*s_prime(1)=positive position mass at every real rough Dirichlet zero. Thus the derivative is nonzero and the analytic order is exactly one. The Banach implicit-function theorem supplies local analytic potential branches, real on nearby real potentials. Open-band exclusion gives the neighboring-band collar criterion for membership in a selected closed gap. The free characteristic is exactly sin(z)/z for nonzero z, equals one at energy zero, and vanishes at every positive free energy (n*pi)^2. A generic compact-interval projection proves closedness of zero existence in continuously varying real closed intervals. Theorem 2 and Theorem 3(ii) remain verified for the exact source Arnold actions. Theorems 1 and 3(i) remain unverified: their physical Birkhoff map and coordinate/action identity are still required. Every real rough Dirichlet zero is now simple, with exact order one and a local analytic potential branch. Exact gap labeling, norming data and the coordinate construction remain essential.
